problem: For the function $f(x,y,z)={x}^{3}+{z}^{2}{y}^{2}+2z$, find a vector that's perpendicular to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,-1,-1).$
worked_solution:
A normal vector to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,-1,-1)$ can be found by computing 
$∇f(1,-1,-1).$ 

So, we first find the gradient and evaluate it at $(x,y,z)=(1,-1,-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\text{ }j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\text{ }k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}+{z}^{2}{y}^{2}+2z)\,i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}+{z}^{2}{y}^{2}+2z)\,j+\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{3}+{z}^{2}{y}^{2}+2z)\,k \\  & =3{x}^{2}\text{ }i+2{z}^{2}y\text{ }j+(2z{y}^{2}+2)\text{ }k \\ ∇f(1,-1,-1) & =3(1)^{2}\,i+2(-1)^{2}(-1)\,j+(2(-1)(-1)^{2}+2)k \\  & =3\,i-2\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $3\,i-2\,j$ is perpendicular to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,-1,-1).$
